Rail Safety Week 2026
 Rail Safety Week will take place across Canada from September 21st to September 27th. 

CN has partnered with Operation Lifesaver Canada (OL) to raise public awareness about the dangers of crossing and trespassing on railway property for more than 20 years. 

CN and OL are asking council to keep communities safe by raising awareness about the critical issue of rail safety. 

CN and OL have provided a Rail Safety Week proclamation for adoption, and ask that it be promoted on social media platforms. 
Recommendation:
Whereas, Rail Safety Week is to be held across Canada from September 21 to 27 2026;
Whereas, 252 railway crossing and trespassing incidents occurred in Canada in 2025; resulting in 69 avoidable fatalities and 60 avoidable serious injuries;
Whereas, educating and informing the public about rail safety (reminding the public that railway rights-of-way are private property, enhancing public awareness of the dangers associated with highway rail grade crossings, ensuring pedestrians and motorists are looking and listening while near railways, and obeying established traffic laws) will reduce the number of avoidable fatalities and injuries cause by incidents involving trains and citizens; and
Whereas, Operation Lifesaver is a public/private partnership whose aim is to work with the public, rail industry, governments, police services, media and others to raise rail safety awareness;
Whereas, CN and Operation Lifesaver have requested Council adopt this resolution in support of its ongoing efforts to raise awareness, save lives and prevent injuries in communities, including our municipality;
Therefore, be it resolved that the Township of Leeds and the Thousand Islands Council do hereby proclaim that the week of September 21 to September 27, 2026 as Rail Safety Week in the Township of Leeds and the Thousand Islands.

Background:
This report presents a proposed Confidential Information Sharing Agreement
("Agreement") received from Alto (VIA HFR – VIA TGF Inc.) for Council's review and
direction. The Agreement would govern the exchange of confidential information
between the Township and Alto in connection with a possible high-speed rail corridor.
Council's direction is sought regarding whether to authorize execution of this
Agreement.
On March 9, 2026, Council adopted Resolution 2026.Council.052 opposing the
proposed Alto High Speed Rail in either of its proposed locations.
Moved: Councillor Mabee
Seconded: Councillor Antoine-Hartley
Whereas Alto, a federal crown corporation, whose role is to establish a high-
speed rail (HSR) network between Toronto and Quebec City has recently
released possible route options; and
Page 1 of 4
Whereas Alto has stated that the proposed southern corridor, in agricultural and
resort areas with higher population density, simplifies construction and
operations; and
Whereas Leeds and the Thousand Islands is surrounded by affected
municipalities and takes pride in the rural character of Eastern Ontario, the
protection of environmentally sensitive areas, agricultural lands and many natural
features including the UNESCO-designated Frontenac Arch Biosphere; and
Whereas the proposal for a high speed rail will divide Canadians and forever
transform the beautiful landscape of the area; and
Whereas Leeds and the Thousand Islands believes that the investment that is
proposed could, and should be allocated towards the current VIA Rail
transportation system to upgrade and better serve the residents of all of Canada;
Therefore, Be It Resolved That the Council of the Township of Leeds and the
Thousand Islands will not support the proposed Alto High Speed Rail in either of
its proposed locations; and
That staff be directed to send this motion to the Hon. Steve Mackinnon, Federal
Minister of Transportation, The Honourable Mark Carney, Prime Minister of
Canada, MP Michael Barrett, Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario, MPP
Steve Clark, and Mark Imbleau, the President of Alto.
Analysis:
On Wednesday July 22, 2026, the Township’s Acting CAO attended a meeting with the
Mayor, United Counties CAO and a representative of Alto. At that meeting questions
were asked about the ongoing route planning and potential locations given the recent
announcement about a potential Kingston stop being planned. It was noted in this
meeting that the Township had concerns about potential land fragmentation and
impacts on properties and public roads in the Township. Questions were also asked
about potential route locations through the Township.
The Alto representative indicated that they would like to start having meetings with local
municipalities in September and that Alto was requesting municipalities to enter into a
Confidential Information sharing Agreement. Staff have received the template
agreement which requires the Township to populate Township specific information prior
to finalizing the agreement (Exhibit A).
Alto has advised that the Agreement is intended to support early, informal technical
discussions between Alto and municipalities along possible corridor evaluation. Alto's
rationale is set out below:
"A Confidential Information Sharing Agreement is a common practice and a standard
tool widely used in the industry to support focused and informed technical discussions
during the early planning stages of an infrastructure project. It ensures that information
Page 2 of 4
shared between parties is treated as confidential while technical work progresses to
avoid premature leaks of plans or information that are still in development.
Why Alto is requesting Confidential Information Sharing Agreements: As planning
advances and discussions move into more detailed technical and alignment
considerations, Alto is engaging municipalities more closely in discussions that involve
early concepts, technical analysis, and emerging ideas that are still being refined. A
confidential information sharing agreement creates an environment where this evolving
information can be shared, supporting more informed and productive collaboration.
What this means for municipalities: For municipalities, a confidential information sharing
agreement enables two-way dialogue. It allows municipal staff to share insights and
data on planning priorities, growth, infrastructure, and community considerations, while
receiving early, non-public information to inform their planning. This mutual
confidentiality supports candid discussions and helps ensure that local perspectives are
understood and reflected as the project evolves."
Execution of the agreement will restrict the ability of the Township to share information.
Should Council choose to proceed with execution of the agreement it will be important
to ensure that the agreement clearly defines what is confidential information.
In the absence of this agreement the Township may have limited/restricted access to
information and technical /discussions regarding proposed routes or alignment before
decisions are finalized. Input maybe limited to formal public consultation opportunities
rather than early information sharing and potential influence or input into route locations
or mitigation of property impacts; and the Township may not have access to the same
information as other municipalities that have executed the agreement.
Staff are seeking Council direction regarding the request from Alto to enter into a
Confidential Information Sharing Agreement with Alto to ensure that planning for the
proposed high-speed rail project appropriately considers the Township's planning
priorities, anticipated growth, infrastructure, and broader community interests.
Alternatives:
Option 1
Advise Alto that Council will not be executing the Confidential Information Sharing
Agreement;
Option 2
Council delegate authority to the Clerk and CAO to execute the agreement subject to
approval of the final scope and terms of the agreement by Township Legal Counsel.
Option 3
Page 3 of 4
Council direct staff to work with Township Legal Counsel to finalize the terms and scope
of the agreement and bring a report to the October Council meeting for further
consideration; or

Memorandum to the City of Markham Committee of Adjustment
September 14, 2026
File: A/029/26
Address: 29 Laidlaw Boulevard, Markham
Applicant: Gregory Design Group (Shane Gregory)
Hearing Date: Wednesday, September 16, 2026
The following comments are provided on behalf of the East Team:
The applicant is requesting relief from the following requirements of By-law 2024-
19, EMP-SE, as amended, to permit a motor vehicle sales establishment which
will be accessory to the existing automotive garage. The requested variance
seeks to permit the following:
a) By-law 2024-19, Section 9.4.2.1:to permit an indoor motor vehicle
sales establishment, whereas the by-law does not permit the use.
BACKGROUND
Property Description
The 4,058 m2 (43,788 ft2) industrial site is located on the southeast corner of
Laidlaw Boulevard and Bullock Drive, west of McCowan Road and north of
Highway 7 (the ‘Subject Property’). The surrounding area to the west and south of
the Subject Property is a mix of commercial and industrial buildings, predominantly
dedicated to automotive garages and services, vehicle rental agencies and
automotive sales. The area to the east of the Subject Property is an established
residential neighbourhood comprised of one and two-storey detached dwellings.
There is an existing two-storey building (1,323 m²) on the Subject Property, which
according to assessment records was constructed in 2001. The ground floor and
east half of the existing building, fronting Bullock Drive, is dedicated to the repair
of motor vehicles. The west half of the building, fronting Laidlaw Boulevard,
includes several smaller units for use by other commercial businesses.
History of the Application
In 2003, a temporary use bylaw (By-law 2003-287) was approved to permit one
motor vehicles sales establishment on the Subject Property. This temporary use
by-law expired in 2006; however, the motor vehicles sales establishment has
continued to operate.
Proposal
The applicant is seeking permission to use a portion of the existing automotive
repair and service garage for an indoor motor vehicle sales establishment as an
accessory use. No changes are being proposed to the exterior of the building or
property. No additional parking spaces are required to facilitate the proposed use.
The applicant is seeking permission to legalize the on-going motor vehicle sales
use.
Official Plan and Zoning
Official Plan 2014 (partially approved on November 24/17, and updated on July
17/24)
The 2014 Official Plan designates the subject property ‘Service Employment’,
which provides for a range of service and retail uses together with light industrial,
warehousing and office uses. The Service Employment policies provide for motor
vehicle sales with limited outdoor storage as a discretionary use that operates as
an accessory to a permitted use. Additional provisions for the motor vehicle retail
sales are identified in Section 8.13.6 of the Official Plan. These polices permit the
sale of associated merchandise and related services in conjunction with a business
located on the same property. Planning staff have had regard for policies of the
Official Plan.
The property is zoned Employment – Service Employment (‘EMP-SE’) under the
Comprehensive Zoning By-law 2024-19. The EMP-SE zone is found in older
employment areas and are typically suited to uses located within multiple unit
buildings that provide goods and services to businesses and residents. The EMP-
SE zone permits a range of motor vehicle businesses uses, including maintenance
shops, fueling stations, washing facilities, repair and body shops, sales and rental
establishments.
Zoning Preliminary Review (ZPR) Undertaken
The Applicant completed a Zoning Preliminary Review (ZPR) on July 27th, 2026 to
confirm the variances required for the proposed development.
COMMENTS
The Planning Act states that four tests must be met in order for a variance to be
granted by the Committee of Adjustment:
a) The variance must be minor in nature;
b) The variance must be desirable, in the opinion of the Committee of
Adjustment, for the appropriate development or use of land, building or
structure;
c) The general intent and purpose of the Zoning By-law must be maintained;
d) The general intent and purpose of the Official Plan must be maintained.
Permit the Indoor Sale of Motor Vehicles
The applicant is requesting a variance to permit a motor vehicle sales
establishment on the subject lands. It is Staff’s understanding that the motor
vehicle sales establishment office is proposed as an accessory use to the storage
and repair of automobiles within the existing building. The Service Employment
policies of the Official Plan provide for motor vehicle sales as discretionary uses
accessory to a permitted use. The sale of motor vehicles in conjunction with the
operation of an automotive garage on the Subject Property conforms to the Service
Employment policies of the Official Plan.
The new Comprehensive Zoning By-law 2014-19 permits motor vehicle sales
establishments only if they lawfully existed before the Zoning By-law was enacted.
Given that the temporary use by-law expired, the continued use of motor vehicle
sales is no longer permitted and therefore requires a minor variance application to
legalize the use. Staff have no objections to the requested variance as it does not
result in any changes or impacts to adjacent properties.
PUBLIC INPUT SUMMARY
No written submissions were received as of September 10, 2026. It is noted that
additional information may be received after the writing of the report, and the
Secretary-Treasurer will provide information on this at the meeting.
CONCLUSION
Planning Staff have reviewed the application with respect to Section 45(1) of The
Planning Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. P.13, as amended, and are of the opinion that the
variance request meets the four tests of the Planning Act and have no objection.
Staff recommend that the Committee consider public input in reaching a decision.
The onus is ultimately on the applicant to demonstrate why they should be
granted relief from the requirements of the zoning by-law, and how they satisfy
the tests of the Planning Act required for the granting of minor variances.
Please refer to Appendix “A” for conditions to be attached to any approval of this
application.

Terms of Reference
Heritage Advisory Committee
A. Mission Statement
The Meaford Heritage Advisory Committee is established by Council for the
purpose of making recommendations to Council on the identification,
conservation and preservation of buildings and landscapes of cultural
heritage value or interest, pursuant to the Ontario Heritage Act.
A. Objectives
Recognizing that heritage is an important part of the fabric of the
Municipality of Meaford, the objectives of the Meaford Heritage Advisory
Committee include the following:
• To foster community pride within the Municipality
• To attract tourism to the Municipality
• To support economic growth through the preservation of Meaford’s
Heritage District
B. General
1. The Meaford Heritage Advisory Committee (HAC) shall be created by
Council By-law which will include these Terms of Reference (TOR).
2. The HAC shall consist of up to seven voting members appointed by
Resolution of Council.
3. The membership shall contain at least one member of Council, who
shall serve as the committee chair, and may contain two members
at the discretion of Council.
4. Where possible, a youth representative may be appointed.

Heritage Advisory Committee Terms of Reference
5. The members of the HAC shall be appointed in accordance with the
Municipality’s Appointments Policy.
6. Members of the HAC will be selected based on a demonstrated
interest in heritage, local knowledge and/or relevant expertise. The
selection process will be open and merit-based, with consideration
given to ensuring diversity and inclusion.
7. No public member of HAC shall be a member of another municipal
committee or Board.
8. The Mayor shall be an ex-officio member of the HAC.
9. The term of office of the members of the HAC shall expire as of
January 31 immediately following each regular municipal election.
C. Definitions
1. “Chair” means the person chairing any meeting of the HAC.
2. “Committee” means the Municipality of Meaford Heritage Advisory
Committee (HAC).
3. “Council” means the Mayor and Council of the Municipality of
Meaford.
4. “Deputation” means a verbal presentation about a subject that is on
the published HAC agenda for that meeting.
5. “ex-officio” means a member that may fully participate in HAC
discussions but cannot vote.
6. “Majority” shall mean more than half of the Members present and
voting on an issue. The count shall include only those present,
including the Chair of the Meeting.
7. “Member” shall mean a person appointed by Municipal Council
Resolution to the HAC and does not include an ex-officio member.
8. “Municipality” shall mean the Municipality of Meaford.
9. “Non-statutory Role” shall mean activities the members of the
Heritage Committee engage in which are not set out in the Ontario

Heritage Act, and may include performing research and advising on
by-laws, programs and policies related to heritage matters.
10. “Presentation” means the verbal and/or visual provision of
information to Council by an individual, community group or
organization.
11. “Procedural By-Law” shall mean the most current By-Law concerning
the Proceedings of Council and its Committees as adopted by
Council.
12. “Public Works” encompass engineering, construction and related
activities carried out by government for the benefit of citizens, and
include the acquisition, leasing, maintenance and disposal of
immovable assets held by the municipality.
13. “Quorum” shall be the number equal to a majority of members of
the whole Committee. (i.e. a quorum is 4 in the case of a 7-member
HAC).
14. “Statutory Role” shall mean the work of the Committee in advising
Council on Heritage matters as set out in the Ontario Heritage Act.
15. “Vice-Chair” shall mean the person who has been selected to the

the Chair in the absence of the Chair. The Vice-Chair shall be elected
from among the members at the inaugural meeting of the HAC then
at the first meeting of each year thereafter.
D. Mandate
The Heritage Advisory Committee has a Statutory Role under the Ontario
Heritage Act, 1990, to provide advice and recommendations to Council. The
Heritage Advisory Committee may also perform a Non-statutory Role, under
the direction of Council.
Statutory Role of the Committee
The Ontario Heritage Act (s. 28) defines the committee's statutory role is
to:

Heritage Advisory Committee Terms of Reference
• Advise and assist the council on all matters relating to the
designation of individual properties under Part IV or heritage
conservation districts under Part V
• Make recommendations on applications to alter, erect, demolish or
remove any buildings or structures on designated properties
• Advise Council on applications to repeal by-laws which designate
individual properties as heritage properties
• Make recommendations to Council whether to enter into heritage
conservation easement agreements or covenants, and
• Advise and assist Council on other heritage matters as Council may
deem appropriate by by-law.
Non-statutory Role
The Heritage Advisory Committee may engage in non-statutory activities
with the aim of heritage preservation, public engagement and awareness
and heritage recognition in the community, including:
• Researching, identifying and evaluating all the properties and areas
that may deserve protection by maintaining an inventory of listed
heritage properties (structures)
• Identifying issues related to designated or listed properties under
the Ontario Heritage Act
• Promoting heritage conservation as well as advising property owners
on appropriate conservation and maintenance practices
• The development of community recognition for architectural
preservation through commemorative initiatives such as plaque
programs, awards for restoration and sympathetic infill development
• Advising Council of new heritage legislation and funding initiatives
• Advising Council on changes to by-laws and policies which may
impact Heritage matters, such as Official Plan policy, Zoning By-law
amendments, Property Standards By-laws and so on.

structure, located at the above noted address. We were retained to specifically evaluate
damages related to the subject vehicle impact loss event. A comprehensive evaluation with

completed.

inspection and assessment of the subject structure, and to retrieve as-built site measurements
for preparation of the enclosed repair specifications. Our evaluation was limited to the areas
directly adjacent to the impact vicinity; we did not access the remainder of the building. At the

system. Exterior walls were primarily assembled with horizontal siding elements, and the roof
was clad with a metal roofing application.

What is a Closed Session?
In Ontario, Councils of a municipality can convene in closed sessions (private meetings) for specific reasons outlined in Section 239 of the Municipal Act, 2001. These reasons typically include:

- Personal matters
- Litigation or potential litigation
- Advice subject to solicitor-client privilege
- Negotiations
- Matters that could reveal confidential information

The purpose of closed sessions is to allow Councils to discuss sensitive matters that require privacy and confidentiality while still ensuring transparency and accountability in the decision-making process. Council typically cannot vote within a closed session unless to direct Staff. Any motions discussed in a closed session are forwarded and voted on in an open session.

Deliberations within closed sessions must remain on-topic and cannot be shared outside the meeting. Closed sessions are only convened as allowed by the Municipal Act.

9. NEW BUSINESS
Support for Local Governance of Conservation Authorities
Moved By: Jamie MacDonald
Seconded By: Carma Williams
Proposed Amendments to the Conservation Authorities Act and ERO #025-1257
WHEREAS the Conservation Authorities Act (1946) enables municipalities to establish
Conservation Authorities and appoint locally elected representatives to their Boards, ensuring
direct municipal oversight and accountability for programs funded by municipal taxpayers;
AND WHEREAS the municipalities within the South Nation River watershed established South
Nation Conservation (SNC) in 1947 to protect people, property, farmland, water resources, and
natural systems through a watershed-based model that reflects local geographic, hydrologic, and
community needs;
AND WHEREAS municipalities within the SNC jurisdiction currently provide between 25% and
50% of total funding for conservation authority operations, while provincial funding has
declined to approximately 3% in recent years;
AND WHEREAS SNC delivers essential services that support municipal responsibilities,
including:
● natural hazard identification and permitting;
● watershed planning and development review;
● flood forecasting, emergency management, and low water response;
● drinking water source protection;
● watershed monitoring, reporting, and technical studies;
● sustainable forestry, agricultural stewardship, and restoration programs;
● management of over 13,000 acres of conservation lands, including lands donated by
residents and managed through municipal service agreements;
AND WHEREAS on November 7, 2025, the Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks
posted ERO #025-1257 proposing to consolidate Ontario’s 36 Conservation Authorities into
seven regional conservation authorities and to establish a new Ontario Provincial Conservation
Agency, with limited consultation and without accompanying cost-benefit analysis or evidence
demonstrating the need for this restructuring;
AND WHEREAS Schedule 3 of Bill 68 enables the Province to assume governance authority over
regional conservation authorities, raising concerns regarding diminished municipal
representation, loss of local decision-making, and centralization of watershed management;
AND WHEREAS municipalities in Eastern Ontario have expressed concern, including the United
Counties of Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry, that restructuring may:
● increase red tape and administrative burden;
● impose significant transition costs for HR, IT, land transfers, and governance realignment;
● dilute rural voices within large regional agencies dominated by major urban centres;
● erode donor confidence and affect the stewardship of thousands of acres of locally
donated lands;
● disrupt bilingual service delivery in designated municipalities governed by the French
Language Services Act;
AND WHEREAS Conservation Authorities—including SNC—already collaborate regionally
through successful shared-service models, joint watershed studies, coordinated flood
forecasting, agricultural stewardship partnerships, digital permitting, and harmonized technical
reviews, demonstrating that modernization and efficiency can be achieved without dismantling
local governance structures;
AND WHEREAS municipalities rely on SNC’s field-based expertise, rapid on-site support,
landowner relationships, and local knowledge—services that risk being weakened under a
large, centralized regional structure;
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Council of Township of North Glengarry urges the
Government of Ontario to maintain local, municipally governed, watershed-based Conservation
Authorities, including South Nation Conservation, to ensure effective natural resource and
natural hazard management, transparent local services, and accountability for municipal levy
dollars;
AND FURTHER THAT this Council does not support the proposed consolidation boundaries
presented in ERO #025-1257 or the creation of a new provincial Conservation Agency without
evidence-based analysis, transparent consultation, and clear articulation of impacts to
municipal budgets, local service delivery, donor lands, and bilingual obligations;
AND FURTHER THAT this Council encourages the Province to work collaboratively with
municipalities and Conservation Authorities to identify opportunities for improved consistency,
modernization, and shared-service approaches within the existing watershed governance
model;
AND FURTHER THAT a copy of this resolution be sent to:
● the Minister of the Environment, Conservation and Parks;
● local MPPs and MPs;
● all municipalities within the South Nation Watershed;
● the Association of Municipalities of Ontario;
● the Rural Ontario Municipal Association;
● Conservation Ontario; and
● all Conservation Authorities in Ontario.
Deferred

MFOA Request for the Permanent Doubling of the Ontario Community
Infrastructure Fund (OCIF) Beyond 2026
WHEREAS recent municipal infrastructure funding programs by the Government of Canada
and Province of Ontario have tended to prioritize growth-related or housing-enabling
infrastructure projects over infrastructure renewal needs;
AND WHEREAS the Government of Ontario has regulated municipal infrastructure asset
management through O. Reg 588/17 (Asset Management Planning for Municipal Infrastructure)
under the Infrastructure for Jobs and Prosperity Act, 2015;
AND WHEREAS municipal asset management plans and the Financial Accountability Office of
Ontario have identified that municipalities have significant state-of-good-repair backlogs and
renewal needs for infrastructure;
AND WHEREAS the Government of Ontario doubled the Ontario Community
Infrastructure Fund (OCIF) from $200M/year to $400M/year for 2021-2026 but has not
publicly committed to maintaining this level of funding beyond 2026;
AND WHEREAS the OCIF has become a vital and indispensable resource for municipalities,
assisting them with improving their asset management programs and meeting community-
preserving infrastructure renewal needs;
AND WHEREAS increased geopolitical uncertainty is threatening the economic prosperity of
Canada, Ontario, and every municipality;
AND WHEREAS municipal infrastructure is a key enabler and preserver of economic
prosperity;
AND WHEREAS the Municipal Finance Officers’ Association of Ontario (MFOA) has heard
from its members and their municipalities concerns regarding the potential erosion of existing
municipal infrastructure and thus service levels in light of the ongoing focus on housing-
enabling infrastructure by grant funding programs;
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that THE MUNICIPALITY OF NORTH MIDDLESEX
supports MFOA’s letter to the Ministry of Infrastructure requesting that the doubling of the
Ontario Community Infrastructure Fund be made permanent in advance of the allocations for
the 2027 calendar year, helping municipalities to continue building housing-enabling
infrastructure while preserving the economic value provided by existing infrastructure.

By-Law No. 2022-83
Being a by-law to appoint an Integrity Commissioner for the Corporation of
Northern Bruce Peninsula
WHEREAS section 223.2 of the Municipal Act, 2001, S.O. 2001, c. 25, as amended,
requires that each municipality in the Province of Ontario establish codes of conduct
for members of its Council and local boards;
AND WHEREAS section 223.3 of the Municipal Act, 2001, S.O. 2001, c. 25, as
amended, requires that each municipality in the Province of Ontario appoint an
Integrity Commissioner, who shall be responsible for performing in an independent
manner the functions assigned by the municipality with respect to any of the matters
referenced in that section
NOW THEREFORE the Council of the Corporation of the Municipality of Northern
Bruce Peninsula enacts as follows:
1. THAT Aird & Berlis LLP is hereby appointed as the Integrity Commissioner for
the Corporation of the Municipality of Northern Bruce Peninsula.
2. THAT the Integrity Commissioner is hereby assigned the functions
assigned by the municipality with respect to the following:
a. The application of the code of conduct for members of council and the code
of conduct for members of local boards;
b. The application of any procedures, rules and policies of the municipality and
local boards governing the ethical behaviour of members of council and of
local boards;
c. The application of sections 5, 5.1 and 5.2 of the Municipal Conflict of
Interest Act to members of council and of local boards;
d. Requests from members of council and of local boards for advice
respecting their obligations under the code of conduct applicable to the
member;
e. Requests from members of council and of local boards for advice
respecting their obligations under a procedure, rule or policy of the
municipality or of the local board, as the case may be, governing the ethical
behaviour of members;
f. Requests from members of council and of local boards for advice
respecting their obligations under the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act, and
g. The provision of educational information to members of council, members of
local boards, the municipality and the public about the municipality's codes
of conduct for members of council and members of local boards and about
the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act.
3. THAT the Integrity Commissioner and any person acting under the instructions
of the Integrity Commissioner is hereby indemnified and saved harmless for
costs reasonably incurred in connection with the defence of a proceeding if the
proceeding relates to an act done in good faith in the performance or intended
performance of a duty or authority under this Part or a by-law passed under it
or an alleged neglect or default in the performance in good faith of the duty or
authority.
4. That the Mayor and Clerk are hereby authorized to execute the Retainer
Agreement between the Corporation of the Municipality of Northern Bruce
Peninsula and Aird Berlis LLP for the purpose of Integrity Commissioner
5. That this By-Law shall be effective until December 31, 2023.
6. That this By-Law shall come into force and take effect immediately upon passing
and By-Law No. 2020-86 is rescinded.
Read a first and second time this 26th day of September 2022.
Read a third time, finally passed, signed and sealed this 26th day of September 2022.

(a) Purpose of the Application:
The applicants are proposing relief from the above-noted provisions of the Township Zoning By-
law to recognize a recently constructed accessory building (approximately 167.2 m2 (1,800 ft2) in
size) and an existing barn that is used for storage (approximately 72.8 m2 (784 ft2) in size). The
total gross floor area of all accessory structures is approximately 240.6 m2 (2,590 ft2) in size,
whereas 170 m2 (1,830 ft2) is permitted in the ‘Residential Existing Zone (RE)’.
Initially, the applicants had agreed to demolish the existing barn structure when the new
accessory building was completed. However, through discussion with the applicants they would
prefer to maintain both structures for personal storage and it was noted that the subject minor
variance would be required.
While the application submitted for the variances requesting a total gross floor area of 263 m2
(2,831 ft2), reviewing the sketch submitted by the applicant, the coverage results in a total of
240.6 m2 (2,590 ft2) and the report will recommend this amended relief to align with the applicants’
drawing.
The subject lands do contain a portion of non-ecologically important woodlands identified in the
Oxford Natural Heritage Systems Study (ONHSS); however, the recently constructed accessory
building is already located within this area and was situated in a way that there was little impact
from the development.
The subject property comprises an area of approximately 0.94 ha (2.32 ac) and currently contains
a single detached dwelling with attached garage, the existing barn and the recently constructed
accessory building.

accessory structure on the subject lands, as well as their setbacks and dimensions.

(d) Intent and Purpose of the Official Plan:
The subject property is located within the Agricultural Reserve designation according to the
Official Plan, which supports a wide range of agricultural type land uses. The Official Plan also
recognizes existing non-farm rural residential uses, together with their accessory buildings on
lands designated as Agricultural Reserve and it is the intent of the Official Plan to ensure that
non-farm rural residential uses shall not hinder surrounding agricultural operations.
Planning staff are generally satisfied that the development of a residential accessory structure will
have minimal impact on surrounding agricultural land uses. As such, staff are of the opinion that
the requested variances are in-keeping with the intent of the Official Plan.
(e) Intent and Purpose of the Zoning By-law:
The subject property is zoned ‘Residential Existing Lot Zone (RE)’, which permits single detached
dwellings and accessory structures thereto.
Accessory structures are permitted on parcels zoned ‘RE’ to a maximum lot coverage of
170 m2 (1,830 ft²) of gross floor area or 10% of the lot area, whichever is lesser. This provision
is intended to ensure such structures remain clearly secondary and ancillary to the main use of
the property and limit impacts on neighbouring properties. This provision also assists to ensure
sufficient space is maintained on the property to accommodate private services, grading/drainage
and amenity space.
In this case, the applicants have recently constructed a new accessory building being
approximately 167.2 m2 (1,800 ft2) but also want to maintain an existing barn structure being
approximately 72.8 m2 (784 ft2), that is being used for personal storage as well. The applicants
had indicated that they would demolish the barn structure after the new building was constructed,
however, the applicants have now submitted the subject application in order to keep both
structures with an increased total lot coverage for all accessory buildings.
Planning staff are satisfied that the subject lands are of sufficient size to provide adequate space
to accommodate the recently constructed accessory structure and existing barn, and given the
proposed location, being setback sufficiently from Slant Road, as well as being located within the
rear yard on the property, staff are satisfied that the proposed accessory structure will remain
secondary and ancillary to the main residential use of the property, provide for all other applicable
setbacks required by the zoning by-law, and provide for amenity space and adequate area for the
provision of private services.

accessory structure and an existing barn structure which results in a cumulative overall gross floor

LOCATION:
The subject lands are described as Lot 11, North side of Main Street, Plan 43, in the Township of
Norwich. The lands are located on the north side of Main Street lying between Grove Street and
Maple Street and are municipally known as 276 Main Street West, Village of Otterville.

Surrounding land uses include low density residential type housing in the village of Otterville. Otter

COMMENTS:
(a) Purpose of the Application:
The applicant is seeking relief from the Township Zoning By-law in order to recognize an existing
legal non-conforming interior side yard width of 0.94 m (3.11 ft). The subject lands previously
contained a one storey dwelling which benefitted from a lesser interior side yard based on the
zoning provisions of previous versions of the zoning by-law. The previous dwelling was recently
razed by fire and the applicants are proposing to replace the dwelling, on the same foundation,
with a two storey dwelling.
Section 5.19.6 of the Zoning By-law does recognize the ability for additions to non-conforming
buildings, provided that the addition does not contravene any other zoning provisions. In this
instance, the addition will contravene the interior side yard setback provisions and therefore the
variance is required to recognize the deficiency.
The subject lands are approximately 1,057.68 m2 (11,386.7 ft2) in area, are currently vacant aside
from the foundation of the previous dwelling. A two storey dwelling is proposed and a detached
garage.
Plate 1, Location Map with Existing Zoning, shows the location of the subject lands and the current
zoning in the immediate vicinity.
Plate 2, Aerial Map (2020), shows the location of the subject lands and surrounding properties,
and the location of the existing bunker silos.
Plate 3, Applicant’s Sketch, illustrates the subject lands and the proposed silo.
(b) Agency Comments
Township of Norwich Fire Department and Oxford County Public Works indicated no concerns
with the subject application.
Township of Norwich Building Department noted that a Real Property Report will be required to
confirm that setback and location of the foundation as it exists.
(c) Public Consultation:
The application was circulated on September 25, 2025, in accordance with the requirements of
the Planning Act. To date, no concerns or objections with the application have been raised.
(d) Intent and Purpose of the Official Plan:
The subject property is located within the Village of Otterville, which is designated ‘Village’
according to the Settlement Strategy Plan for the County of Oxford, and ‘Settlement’ according to
the Township of Norwich Land Use Plan. Within these designations, a range of land uses are
permitted, with the exception of multiple unit residential development involving more than two
units.

Planning staff are generally satisfied that the construction of single detached dwelling is in keeping
with the Settlement policies of Official Plan.
(e) Intent and Purpose of the Zoning By-law:
The subject lands are currently zoned ‘Residential Type 1 Zone (R1)’, according to the Township
of Norwich Zoning By-law. Permitted uses within the R1 zone include a single detached dwelling,
home occupation, a group home, and accessory buildings/structures.
The provisions of the R1 zone require a minimum lot area of 2,800 m2 (30,140 ft2) where sanitary
sewers are not available, minimum lot depth of 50 m (164 ft), front yard depth of 7.5 m (24.6 ft),
rear yard depth of 7.5 m (24.6 ft), exterior side yard width of 7.5 m (24.6 ft) and an interior side
yard width of 1.5 m (4.9 ft). Properties within the R1 zone are permitted a maximum lot coverage
of 30%.
The existing foundation has an approximate interior side yard setback of 0.94 m (3.11 ft), the
previous version of the zoning by-law (1976) permitted an interior side yard of 1.2 m (4 ft) which
is why the foundation exists as it does. The previous one storey dwelling would have benefitted
from a legal non-conforming status when the current zoning by-law (2003) was passed. When the
existing dwelling was razed by fire, it could have been replaced by another one storey dwelling,
however, the applicants are proposing a two storey dwelling instead.
As noted, Section 5.19.6 does permit the extension or addition to a non-conforming use, building
or structure, provided that the extension or addition does not contravene any of the zone
provisions of the Zoning By-law. As the applicants are proposing a two storey dwelling, the
addition of another storey is contravening the zoning provisions, specifically the required interior
side yard width.
Side yard width provisions are intended to ensure that there is adequate space for the
maintenance of the property, proper drainage, and appropriate access to the remainder of the
property. The applicant is proposing a setback of 0.94 m (3.11 ft) which would recognize the
location of the existing foundation. Staff are satisfied that the proposed setback is sufficient to
allow for access around the dwelling and for drainage and maintenance purposes.
(f) Desirable Development/Use:
The application for minor variance has been requested to facilitate the construction of a two storey
dwelling in place of a one storey razed by fire.
Staff are satisfied that the proposed interior side yard setback will recognize an existing legal non-
conforming foundation and permit an additional storey to be constructed.

considered to be minor in nature, desirable for the appropriate development and use of the land
and in-keeping with the general intent and purpose of the Zoning By-law and the objectives and
policies of the Official Plan with respect to accessory structures.

1.2 County of Oxford Growth Forecast Area Municipal and
Settlement Area Allocations
Building on the County-wide forecasts provided in Section 1.1, population, housing, and
employment allocations by Area Municipality were developed. These allocations have
been based on a detailed review of the following local supply and demand factors:
Local Supply Factors
• Supply of potential future housing stock in the development approvals process by
housing structure type, approval status, and location;
• Current inventory of net vacant designated “greenfield” lands not currently in the
development approvals process;
• Residential intensification opportunities;
• Supply of designated vacant Employment Area lands by Area Municipality;
• Consideration of water and wastewater servicing capacity; and
• Provincial, County, and Area Municipal policy direction regarding forecast
residential growth by Settlement Area and Rural Area.
Demand Factors
• Historical population, housing, and employment trends based on Statistics
Canada (Census) data by Area Municipality;
• A review of recent residential and non-residential building permit data by housing
structure type and employment sector by Area Municipality;
• Historical commuting trends and anticipated employment growth opportunities
within the surrounding market area;
• A review of local employment opportunities by sector and Area Municipality.
• Forecast population trends by major age group and associated household
formation trends by age of household maintainer;
• Consideration of long-term housing needs by housing tenure (i.e. ownership vs.
rental housing) and influence on housing demand by structure type; and
• Housing market demand by Area Municipality across all major demographic
groups, including young adults, new families, move-up buyers, and empty
nesters/seniors.

Oxford County 2024 - Growth Analysis and Land Needs Assessment Package - September 10 2025
While population and employment growth rates vary significantly by geographic area,
each of the Area Municipalities within the County share several common attributes with
respect to near- and longer-term population growth and development trends. These
include the following:
• All Area Municipalities are forecast to experience higher total annual population
housing and employment growth relative to historical trends experienced
between 2011 and 2021.
• Continued regional employment opportunities, particularly those related to
manufacturing; goods movement; agricultural; as well other service-producing
and knowledge-based sectors, represent a key driver of future employment
growth within the County and its Area Municipalities.
• Declining housing affordability, combined with a range of broader economic
headwinds, including persistently high inflation rates, rising household debt, U.S.
protectionist policy, and a slower short-term economic outlook at the national,
provincial and regional level are anticipated to dampen housing demand in the
near term (i.e., next 12 to 24 months), relative to recent historical highs
experienced during the past five years.
• Over the longer term (i.e., 10+ years), the average rate of annual housing
development is anticipated to gradually slow (relative the medium-term forecast
period i.e. next decade) across all Area Municipalities within the County, driven
by modestly slower regional and provincial economic growth associated with an
aging population and regional labour force.
• Low-density housing forms are forecast comprise a notable share of future
housing growth; however, increasing market demand will exist for medium- and
high-density housing types across all Area Municipalities.

This procedure has been created to establish a protocol for public participation in electronic
Council and Planning Public Meetings in the Township of Oro-Medonte in accordance with
Section 238 (3.3) of the Municipal Act, 2001, the Planning Act, 1990, c.P.13. and the
Emergency Management and Civil Protection Act. This procedure also outlines the public
responsibility in order to participate in an electronic meeting via telephone or video.
Scope:
The procedure applies to all members of the public, applicants, consultants and delegates
wishing to participate in an electronic Council or Planning Public Meeting, either via video or
telephone. Nevertheless, this policy is subject to rules of procedure as stated in the
Procedural By-law and other Provincial legislation.

Video Conferencing Solutions – an electronic meeting platform
Chair – Mayor or Designate

in the capacity of the Clerk in his/her absence, or a person who the Clerk has delegated
authority to in accordance with Section 228(4) of the Municipal Act, 2001, as amended.
IT – Information Technology Division
Share Screen Viewing – two or more applications visible on screen at once (eg. Power Point

 "WHEREAS the rising cost of living and rapid inflation are putting significant financial pressure on individuals and families, especially those living in poverty;

AND WHEREAS residents on programs such as Ontario Works receive maximum fixed monthly incomes of $733, and ODSP recipients receive $1,376;

AND WHEREAS people living with low income are more likely to be renters and the Community Foundation Focus on Housing report found that in 2021 more than 40% of homes in Owen Sound are rented;

AND WHEREAS rent is considered affordable when it is no more than 30% of gross annual income and the 2021 census reports that 38.3% of tenant households in Owen Sound are spending more than 30% of their income on housing;

AND WHEREAS as of March 31, 2024, there 1,650 Grey County households on the Community Housing Waitlist including only those who presently reside in the area;

AND WHEREAS the 2023 Grey County Housing Action Plan identified the need to advocate to the Provincial and Federal governments for housing solutions which may relate to “the ‘income’ side of the housing affordability equation, for example relating to minimum and living wages [and] social benefits (e.g., ODSP; OW)”;

AND WHEREAS poverty also increases food insecurity which negatively impacts physical and mental health especially for children and adequate income is an important social determinant of health that greatly impacts food security;

AND WHEREAS in 2023, the Salvation Army food bank use rose by 42% in Owen Sound and annual meals provided by OSHARE increased 18.6% or 23,000 meals from 2022;

AND WHEREAS in the 2024 Monitoring Food Affordability in Grey Bruce report on food insecurity, Grey Bruce Public Health calls on municipalities to “advocate for federal and provincial government policies (e.g.., increases to income tax credits for low-income households) and programs (e.g., basic income guarantee) to ensure an adequate and secure income for all in Canada”;

AND WHEREAS in February 2024 the Grey Bruce Poverty Task Force issued a call for income solutions to food insecurity;

AND WHEREAS neither municipal governments nor the non-profit sector have the resources to address the root causes of poverty on their own;

AND WHEREAS decreasing poverty levels benefits individuals and their communities by reducing reliance on food banks, social services, health care, emergency services, and other supports as well as improving quality of life and creating positive local economic impacts;

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT City Council join other municipalities across Ontario to urge the Federal and Provincial governments to increase social assistance rates for Ontario Works and the Ontario Disability Support Program and to establish a Guaranteed Livable Income program;

AND THAT this resolution be sent to the Prime Minister, the Premier, the leaders of all parties sitting at Queen’s Park, the Minister of Children, Community and Social Services, the Minister of Health, the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, Alex Ruff, MP for Bruce-Grey-Owen Sound, and Rick Byers, MPP for Bruce-Grey-Owen Sound requesting a response;

AND FURTHER THAT this resolution also be shared with Grey County, Bruce County, the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM), the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO), and the Western Ontario Wardens’ Caucus (WOWC)."

Procedural Bylaw No. 4507(2022)
Being a bylaw to govern the proceedings of the Town of Pelham Council, its Committees, the conduct of its Members and the calling of Meetings.
Procedural By-law No. 4507(2022) was adopted on January 30, 2022, repealing and replacing Bylaw No. 4107(2019), as amended.
This By-law directs regular meetings of Council to be held on the first and third Wednesday of the month, commencing at 9:00 a.m. Public Meetings under the Planning Act are to be scheduled on the second Wednesday of the month, commencing at 5:30 p.m. Dates are subject to change to accommodate various Statutory Holidays, World Religious Holidays, major conferences and other known events. Please refer to the Council Meeting Schedule for approved meeting dates.
Additional notable changes include a new curfew of 1 pm, restructuring of regular meetings of Council to include Committee within Council, hybrid meeting participation, increase of three (3) to four (4) delegations permitted with a five (5) minute time limit, re-classification of Committees to include Statutory, Advisory and Volunteer Working Groups, a delegation submission deadline of ten (10) days prior to the meeting and the requirement to post agendas to the public five (5) days prior to the date of the meeting, being the Friday.

Delegation Request
In accordance with the Procedure By-law, Requests to Appear before Council shall be submitted in the prescribed form no later than 12:00 pm noon ten (10) days prior to the meeting. To: Members of the Peterborough Public Library Board
From: Melissa Redden, Library Director and CEO
Meeting Date: September 15, 2026
Report: 2025 Audit, Report PPL26-048
Subject
A report to inform the Library Board of the Audited 2025 financial statements.
Recommendations
That the Library Board approve the recommendations outlined in Report PPL26-048,
dated September 15, 2026, of the Library Director and CEO as follows:
a) That a verbal report to inform the Library Board of the status of the Library’s
accounts by the Auditor be received for information.
b) That the Peterborough Public Library Board approves the transfer of $30,501
from the Library Surplus Reserve to the 2025 Library Operating budget.
Background
A representative from the Library's auditor will attend the September 15, 2026, Library
Board meeting to present a verbal report on the progress and status of the 2025
financial audit.
During the audit review, it was identified that $30,501 should be transferred from the
Library's surplus reserve to the operating budget to align with the finalized year-end

 WHEREAS the Auto Mayors work collaboratively at the provincial and federal orders of government to promote awareness, advocacy and strategic policy initiatives that strengthen the Canadian economy through advancements and investments in the automotive sector;
WHEREAS continued progress toward tariff-free access to the U.S. market and maintaining an integrated North American auto sector remain the auto sector’s top priority;
WHEREAS the Auto Mayors welcome ongoing collaboration with the Province and the Federal government on greenhouse gas regulations and electrification targets and policies that reflect current market demand, infrastructure readiness and alignment with the U.S.;
WHEREAS the Auto Mayors are ready to work with Federal partners on a coordinated approach to global competition that ensures Canada remains an attractive destination for investment;
WHEREAS strengthening domestic production requires aligning tariff remission frameworks with manufacturing levels and strengthening Buy Ontario procurement policies to ensure public sector fleet purchasing continues to support Ontario based manufacturers;
AND WHEREAS regular review and monitoring of industrial electricity rates, including how domestic rates compare to export rates, will help ensure Ontario manufacturers remain competitive and positioned for growth.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the City of Peterborough, as a member of the Auto Mayors Caucus, support the Auto Mayors’ continued efforts to highlight the automotive sector’s local economic impact, including jobs, supply chains, and community stability, while supporting the automotive ecosystem through business retention and economic development efforts;

The application for Zoning By-law Amendment accompanied by a planning justification
report proposes to the zoning from I – Institutional and R4 – Fourth Density Residential

hall, apartment building and personal service business while recognizing the existing
location of the building, and allowing for a reduction in lot area per unit, minimum floor
area for a unit and parking. These changes are being sought to permit the conversion
from an institutional building into a 22-unit apartment building with a hall and office space
on the property.

NYON OIL INC.
(hereinafter collectively referred to as “Nyon”)
OF THE FIRST PART
- and -
THE CORPORATION OF THE CITY OF PORT COLBORNE

OF THE SECOND PART
WHEREAS Nyon is working towards developing an energy park on the lands described
in Schedule “A” attached hereto in the City of Port Colborne (the “Tank Farm Lands”),
AND WHEREAS in contemplation of the commencement of development of the energy
park, and in compliance with the Site-Specific Zoning By-law, Nyon has prepared a Risk
Assessment Plan (attached hereto as Schedule “B”) and Fire Emergency Plan (attached hereto as
Schedule “C”) (the Risk Assessment Plan and the Fire Emergency Plan are collectively referred
to herein as the “Safety Reports”),
AND WHEREAS the City and Nyon wish to agree on certain matters regarding the
implementation, and the cost of implementing the recommendations set out in the Safety Reports
NOW THEREFORE THIS AGREEMENT WITNESSETH that in consideration of the
mutual covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth, and for other good and valuable
consideration and the sum of Two Dollars ($2.00) of lawful money now paid by each of the parties
to the other (the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby expressly acknowledged), the parties
hereby confirm that the above recitals are true and correct and hereby covenant and agree to and
with each other as follows:
IMPLEMENTATION
1. Nyon acknowledges that it is responsible for implementing the recommendations that are
contained in the Risk Assessment Plan in order to mitigate risk, to improve safety, and to
prevent the unwanted release of hazardous materials.
2. Nyon acknowledges that it is responsible to implement the recommendations that are
contained in the Fire Emergency Plan in order to mitigate risk and respond to fire and other
emergencies on the Tank Farm Lands.
2
3. The parties acknowledge that the Safety Reports are living documents, and as the detailed
plans and engineered drawings are developed for the Tank Farm Lands, accordingly there
may be amendments to the Safety Reports, as appropriate.
COSTS
4. Nyon acknowledges that it is wholly responsible for the cost of the implementation and the
ongoing performance of all recommendations contained in the Risk Assessment Plan
(collectively, the “Risk Assessment Plan Obligations”). The City shall not bear any of
the cost of risk mitigation set out in the Risk Assessment Plan. Nyon hereby indemnifies
and saves harmless the City, its employees, contractors and agents from any and all costs,
losses, actions and other liabilities that the City may incur in connection with, or resulting
from, Nyon’s failure to comply with or carry out the Risk Assessment Plan Obligations.
5. Nyon acknowledges that it is wholly responsible for the cost of the implementation and the
ongoing performance of all recommendations contained in the Fire Emergency Plan
(collectively, the “Fire Emergency Plan Obligations”). The City shall not bear any of the
cost of risk mitigation set out in the Fire Emergency Plan. Nyon hereby indemnifies and
saves harmless the City, its employees, contractors and agents from any and all costs,
losses, actions and other liabilities that the City may incur in connection with, or resulting
from, Nyon’s failure to comply with or carry out the Fire Emergency Plan Obligations.
6. Without limiting the obligations set out in paragraphs 4 and 5 above, Nyon agrees to pay
the training costs for municipal employees as required by the Safety Plans, currently
estimated to be $408,770, in accordance with the following schedule:
(a) $204,335 on application to the City for site plan approval; and
(b) $204,335 on application to the City for a building permit related to the Tank Farm
Lands.
7. Upon receipt of payment from Nyon, as stated in section 6 above, the City shall be
responsible for administering the training of municipal employees in accordance with the
Risk Assessment Plan and the Fire Emergency Plan.
DEFAULT
8. The occurrence of any one or more of the following events is an “Even of Default” within
the meaning of this Agreement:
(a) Nyon is not in compliance with the Risk Assessment Plan Obligations;
(b) Nyon is not in compliance with the Fire Emergency Plan Obligations;
(c) Nyon is not in compliance with any covenant, term or provision of this Agreement;
and

(d) Nyon makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or assigns in bankruptcy or
takes the advantage in respect of its own affairs of any statute for relief in
bankruptcy, moratorium, settlement with creditors, or similar relief of bankrupt or
insolvent debtors, or if a receiving order is made against Nyon, or if Nyon is
adjudged bankrupt or insolvent, or if a liquidator or receiver is appointed by reason
of any actual or alleged insolvency, or any default of Nyon under any mortgage or
other obligation, or if the Tank Farm Lands or interest of Nyon in the Tank Farm
Lands becomes liable to be taken or sold by any creditors or under any writ of
execution or other like process
Upon the occurrence of an Event of Default, the City will provide written notice of the
Event of Default to Nyon (a “Default Notice”). If the Event of Default has not been cured
in its entirety on or before the date which is five (5) days after the Default Notice has been
delivered to Nyon, then the City may, in addition to such other remedies as the City may
have under this Agreement, in law or otherwise, send a notice to Nyon ordering it to
immediately cease all operations on the Tank Farm Lands or to impose such other
restrictions and conditions on the use of the Tank Farm Lands as the City may, in its
absolute discretion, acting reasonably, impose for purposes of protection of the public (a
“Default Order”).
9. Nyon acknowledges that an occurrence of an Event of Default would result in damages and
harm to the City that the City may not be adequately compensated for such damages by
monetary award alone. Accordingly, Nyon agrees that in the event of any such breach, and
in addition to any other remedies available under this Agreement, in law or otherwise, the City
shall be entitled as a matter of right to apply to a court of competent jurisdiction for relief by
way of injunction, restraining order, decree or otherwise as may be appropriate to ensure
compliance by Nyon with the provisions of this Agreement, including without limitation, any
Default Order that may be issued by the City. Any remedy expressly set out in this Agreement
shall be in addition to and not inclusive of or dependent upon the exercise of any other remedy
available at law or otherwise.
SITE PLAN APPROVAL AUTHORITY
10. Nyon acknowledges and agrees that the implementation, cost, and performance of the
recommendations set out in the Safety Reports are properly the subject matter of a site plan
agreement and Nyon covenants that it will not raise any jurisdictional issues with respect
to these matters being incorporated into a site plan agreement under s. 41 of the Planning
Act, RSO 1990, c P.13, and therefore site plan approval is contingent upon the City being
satisfied with the proposed method of implementation of the recommendations set out in
the Safety Reports by Nyon.
11. Nyon acknowledges that the Risk Assessment Plan obligations and the Fire Emergency
Plan obligations will be incorporated into a site plan agreement and, in addition to any
other remedies that the City may have under this Agreement, in law or otherwise, can be
enforced under the site plan agreement and that these obligations will bind the registered
owners of the land.
4
BUILDING PERMITS and DEVELOPMENT
12. No petroleum or petroleum product shall be sold, stored, supplied, distributed, shipped or
otherwise received or removed from the Tank Farm Lands by any means of transportation
or shipment, including without limitation, by ship, rail, truck or pipe prior to the
implementation of the recommendations set out in the Safety Reports, or otherwise agreed
to in writing between the parties.
13. Development of the Tank Farm Lands shall comply with the provisions set out in the Fire

applicable with respect to fire safety and risk management of petroleum and petroleum

4.1 Zoning By-law
The subject property is zoned Rural (RU). Through the proposal, the applicant is seeking to
change the zoning classification to Rural Special Exception (RU-X) to permit the proposed small
scale restaurant use ancillary to the bed and breakfast use established on the property. The
proposed restaurant use is to be wholly located within a portion of the existing dwelling that
contains the residential kitchen and eating area, with a bathroom. Staff recommend that the area
of the lot to receive the site specific zoning exemption should be reduced from the full parcel as
requested, to an area surrounding the dwelling and parking areas as shown in Figure 6. Reducing
the area to the smaller portion of the lot instead of broadly permitting this use on the parcel will
maintain the intent of the proposal to provide for this additional use within the existing dwelling
and limit the development to a future restaurant elsewhere on the property as of right.
Discussions have occurred between the agent and the Chief Building Official regarding the
building classification, and requirements to operate within the building. These discussions outlined
that no work is required for the building due to the small scale nature of the proposal. Since these
discussions, information has been provided regarding the septic system sizing requirements for
the use, in which the engineer outlines the use will increase the required daily flow. Using the
Township’s records, the Chief Building Official has outlined that the septic system is undersized
and will need to be upgraded prior to the use occurring within the building. This upgrade is
recommended to be a condition of the site plan approval since there is no trigger through building
permits to require since no work to the physical building for the use is required.
As mentioned, the restaurant is proposed to be ancillary to the existing bed and breakfast
use on the property to provide meals for bed and breakfast guests and their invited guests. Meals
are permitted to be provided in a bed and breakfast as of right, for guests of the bed and breakfast
as per the definition of a bed and breakfast in the ZBL (S. 2.17):
“Bed and Breakfast shall mean a home occupation conducted in an owner occupied dwelling
in which no more than three guest rooms are made available for overnight accommodation of the
travelling or vacationing public, and in which the proprietor may offer lodging and other meals,
related services, facilities or amenities for guests. A bed and breakfast shall not include any other
establishment otherwise defined or classified herein.”
The proposal seeks to permit additional guests not staying in the bed and breakfast
establishment to be served meals, for a total of 10 guests per dinner (4 Bed and Breakfast guests,
and 6 other guests). As this proposal to accommodate additional customers within the framework
of an existing establishment to promote farm-to-table experiences for bed and breakfast guests
to share with non-overnight friends, staff believe that the proposed small scale restaurant use
maintains the rural intent of the Zoning By-law, rather than a commercial zone.

COUNCIL MEETINGS
Council meetings are a key part of local government, providing residents with the opportunity to observe decision-making, stay informed, and participate in the democratic process. The Township of Schreiber is committed to open, transparent, and accessible governance.
This page outlines when Council meets, how to attend meetings, how to speak to Council, and where to find related information and records.
COUNCIL & COMMITTEE OF THE WHOLE MEETING SCHEDULE
Council and Committee of the Whole meetings are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month at 6:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at the Schreiber Municipal Office. Meeting dates may occasionally change due to statutory holidays, scheduling conflicts, or special circumstances. Residents are encouraged to review the meeting agenda in advance to confirm the meeting date, time, and location.
Members of the public are welcome to attend Council meetings to observe local decision-making and stay informed about municipal initiatives and community matters.
Visit the Agendas & Minutes page to view upcoming agendas and approved meeting minutes.

AGENDAS & MINUTES
Agendas and minutes are published to provide residents with transparent access to the decisions and discussions of Council and its Committees. Agendas are typically posted approximately one week prior to each meeting. Minutes are posted after they have been reviewed and formally approved by Council.
Residents are encouraged to review agendas to stay informed about upcoming discussions and to read approved minutes for official records of Council decisions.
COUNCIL AGENDAS
Council agendas outline the items that will be discussed at upcoming meetings of Council. These documents provide an overview of reports, presentations, bylaws, and other matters requiring Council discussion or decision.
Agendas are typically posted approximately one week before each meeting to allow residents time to review upcoming municipal business.

MEETING MINUTES
Meeting minutes provide the official record of Council meetings. They summarize discussions, motions, resolutions, and decisions made by Council. Minutes are reviewed and approved at a subsequent Council meeting before being published as the official record.

THE CORPORATION OF THE TOWNSHIP OF SCHREIBER
BYLAW 13-2019
BEING A BYLAW TO APPOINT AN INTEGRITY COMMISSIONER
WHEREAS the Municipal Act, S.O. 2001, Chapter 25, Section 223.3 (1), authorizes the
municipality to appoint an Integrity Commissioner who reports to Council and who is
responsible for performing in an independent manner the functions assigned by the
municipality with respect to,
(a) the application of the code of conduct for members of Council and the code of conduct
for members of local boards or of either of them;
(b) the application of any procedures, rules and policies of the municipality and local boards
governing the ethical behaviour of members of council and of local boards or of either of
them.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT THE COUNCIL OF THE CORPORATION
OF THE TOWNSHIP OF SCHREIBER ENACTS AS FOLLOWING:
1) That Expertise for Municipalities (E4m) shall be appointed and act as Integrity
Commissioner.
2) That this appointment shall be subject to the executed Letter of Engagement,
attached as Appendix “A” of this Bylaw.
3) This Bylaw shall come into force and effect upon enactment.
4) This Bylaw may be cited as “Township of Schreiber Integrity Commissioner Bylaw
13-2019”.
Read a first and second time this 26th day of March, 2019.
Read a third time and finally enacted, this 26th day of March, 2019.

The Corporation of the Township of
Smith-Ennismore-Lakefield
By-law No. 2010-045
Being a By-law to Regulate and Restrict Water Use for the Users of the
Lakefield Area Water System and for the Users of the Woodland Acres Area
Water System
Whereas the Ontario Municipal Act, 2001, S.O. 2001, c. 25, Section 2, as
amended, states that municipalities are created by the Province of Ontario to be
responsible and accountable governments with respect to matters within their
jurisdiction, and as such, municipalities are given powers and duties under this
Act, and many other Acts, for the purpose of providing good government with
respect to those matters; and
Whereas the Ontario Municipal Act, 2001, S.O. 2001, c. 25, Section 5.3, as
amended, states that a municipal power shall be exercised by By-law unless the
municipality is specifically authorized to do otherwise; and
Whereas, the water systems servicing the Lakefield Area and the Woodland
Acres Area may have difficulty meeting the daily demands for water during
certain periods of the year; and
Whereas; the Township of Smith-Ennismore-Lakefield passed By-law No. 2002-
68, being a By-law to regulate and restrict the use of water supplied to the users
of the Lakefield Area water system and the Woodland Acres Area water system
and now deems it advisable to repeal stated By-law;
Now Therefore, the Council of the Corporation of the Township of Smith-
Ennismore-Lakefield hereby enacts as follows:
1. That, in the Lakefield Area, from May 15th to September 15th of each year,
those premises with addresses ending with an even number be permitted to
water their lawns and gardens on calendar dates ending with an even number
between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. and between the hours of 6:00
p.m. and 10:00 p.m.
2. That, in the Lakefield Area, from May 15th to September 15th of each year,
those premises with addresses ending with an odd number may be permitted
to water their lawns and gardens on calendar dates ending with an odd
number between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. and between the hours
of 6:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m.
3. That, in the Woodland Acres Area, from June 1st to August 31st of each year,
those premises with addresses ending with an even number be permitted to
water their lawns and gardens on calendar dates ending with an even number
between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.
4. That, in the Woodland Acres Area, from June 1st to August 31st of each year,
those premises with addresses ending with an odd number may be permitted
to water their lawns and gardens on calendar dates ending with an odd
number between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.
5. Notwithstanding Section 1, 2, 3, and 4 of this By-law, watering of newly
seeded or sodded lawns shall be permitted on any day between the hours of
7:00 a.m. and 9:00 a.m. and between the hours of 6:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m.
with a hand held hose until such time as the seed or sod is established.
6. Notwithstanding Section 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5 of this By-law, in the event of an
emergency situation, whereby normal water volumes and pressures are
jeopardized, or where extraordinary circumstances warrant, the Chief
Administrative Officer of the Township of Smith-Ennismore-Lakefield, or
his/her designate, in consultation with the system operator, shall be
authorized and directed to take whatever steps necessary to alleviate the
problem, which may include changes to the existing water restrictions and/or
a total ban on lawn and garden watering.
7. That no other high volume uses of water shall be permitted except under the
direction and control of the Township of Smith-Ennismore-Lakefield.
8. Violation of any of the provisions of this By-law shall constitute an offence.
9. A surcharge in the amount of $50.00 shall be imposed upon the account of
any customer that is found using water in violation of any of the provisions of
this By-law.
10. That each day on which any violation described in the By-law is continued
shall constitute a separate offence and the surcharge provided for under
Section 9 will apply once for each day that such violation occurs.
11. That this By-law applies to all customers of the water systems servicing the
Lakefield Area and the Woodland Acres Area.
12. That the Township of Smith-Ennismore-Lakefield By-law No. 2002-68 is
hereby repealed in its entirety.
13. That this By-law shall come in to full force and effect on the date of passing
thereof.
Read a first, second and third time and finally passed this 15th day of June A.D.,
2010.

The Corporation of the
Township of Selwyn
By-law 2022-084
Procedure By-law
Being a By-law
To Govern the Proceedings of
Council and Committees or Local Board of the
Corporation of the Township of Selwyn
Whereas pursuant to Section 238 of the Municipal Act, 2001, as amended, every
municipality and local board shall pass a procedure By-law for governing the calling, place
and proceedings of meetings;
Now Therefore the Council of the Corporation of the Township of Selwyn Enacts as
follows;
Definitions
1. In this By-law:
a) “Abstain” means a member who is lawfully entitled to vote but chooses not to
exercise their right to vote on a matter, and in such cases in abstention shall be
deemed as a negative vote (Municipal Act S. 246. (2)).
b) “Clerk” means the Clerk of the Corporation of the Township of Selwyn.
c) “Committee” means any advisory or other Committee, subcommittee or similar
entity of which at least 50 per cent of the members are also members of one or
more councils or local boards. A local board does not include police services
boards or public library boards (Municipal Act S. 238. (1)).
d) “Council” means the Council of the Corporation of the Township of Selwyn.
e) “Electronic Participation” includes telephone, video, audio or audio-visual conferencing,
or any other interactive method whereby Members, staff and the public are able to hear
the Member(s) participating by electronic means and the Member(s) participating by
electronic means are able to hear other Members, staff and the public.
f) “Head of Council” means the Mayor of the Corporation of the Township of Selwyn.
g) “Live streaming” is a method of providing video over the internet in real time. The
video stream can be saved and archived allowing those with internet access the
ability to view recordings at their convenience.
h) “Meeting” means any regular, special, committee or other meeting of a Council, or
of a local board or of a committee of either of them, where,
(a) a quorum of members is present, and
(b) members discuss or otherwise deal with any matter in a way that materially
advanced the business or decision-making of the Council, local board or Committee
(Municipal Act S. 238 (1).
i) “Pecuniary Interest” means a direct or indirect pecuniary interest of a member of
Council within the meaning of the Municipal Conflict of Interest Act, R.S.O. 1990, as
amended.
j) “Presiding Officer” means the member of Council who, as determined under Section
12, 13 or 17 of this By-law, is responsible to preside over or act as the Chairperson
of a meeting.
